title: Liudprand of Cremona
fact_summary: A historian whose Antapodosis, written around 958–962, tells of the Hungarians' raids in Italy and the West.

claims.text: The Mapping Medieval Peoples database dates the Antapodosis to 958–962.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the database record says, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: The work looks back over a long period: the database dates the events of book I, chapter 5 to 870–887 and those of book V, chapter 19 to 943.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the database record says, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: In book V he addresses a reader whose king lived at Córdoba (“in qua rex vester moratur, Cordobam”).
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: In book II he tells of the Hungarians' victory over King Berengar's army on the river Brenta, and of King Henry's victory over them near Merseburg.

sources.locator: Antapodosis II.9–15 and II.28–31 (Dümmler ed., pp. 32–35, 39–40)

claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the scanned edition linked under Sources; the English is Claude's own rendering.

open_questions.text: Who was the reader in Spain, and why did Liudprand write for him?
